backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:149 (check_redirect_uri_allowed) — the same-origin relative-path fast-path `if raw.starts_with('/') && !raw.starts_with("//") { return Ok(()) }` blocks protocol-relative `//evil.com` but NOT the backslash variant `/\evil.com` (nor `/\/evil.com`). A user-supplied redirect_uri of `/\evil.com` passes the allowlist as a 'relative path', is stored, re-validated at callback (still passes), and handed straight to `Redirect::temporary(&redirect_uri)` at routes/sso.rs:338, emitting `Location: /\evil.com`. Per the WHATWG URL spec browsers normalise backslashes to forward slashes for http(s) URLs, so `/\evil.com` resolves to `//evil.com` = `https://evil.com` -> open redirect on the post-login SSO flow (phishing / OAuth-code interception vector). The regression test block at routes/sso.rs:1681-1686 covers `//evil.com` but has NO backslash case, so CI is green. Fix: reject any raw whose first two chars normalise to a leading `//` (e.g. also block `starts_with("/\\")`), or parse-and-reject when url::Url::parse(raw) yields a host. Traced entry (login handler ~sso.rs:71 and callback ~sso.rs:204) -> validate -> Redirect; reachable in production.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/users/mod.rs:251 (UserHandler::login) — non-existent email and wrong password both correctly return the generic `"Invalid email or password"`, but a registered SSO-only account (user found, password_hash == None) returns a DISTINCT message via `.ok_or("Account uses SSO login")?`. routes/users.rs:204 (login handler) forwards that raw message verbatim as the 401 body. An attacker can therefore enumerate which emails are registered SSO accounts (distinct response = SSO account exists) — an account-existence disclosure that the generic path was specifically written to prevent. It also short-circuits before the argon2 verify, adding a timing side-channel. Fix: return the same generic `"Invalid email or password"` (log the SSO-account distinction server-side only).

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/actions/api_call.rs:179 (validate_external_url) — the private/internal-IP guard only runs when the host is a LITERAL IP (`if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<IpAddr>()`). A DNS hostname that resolves to a private/link-local/metadata IP (e.g. 169.254.169.254, 10.x, fc00::/7) is not a literal IP, is not in the small blocked_hosts denylist, and does not end in .local/.internal, so it passes validation; reqwest then resolves it at send time (validate-then-resolve TOCTOU / DNS-rebinding SSRF). The URL is not admin-static: execute() (line ~240) runs context.substitute_template(&api_config.url) over trigger data before validation. Failure scenario: a workflow api_call action with url 'http://<attacker-host>/' where <attacker-host> resolves to the cloud metadata endpoint reaches internal infra; the IPv6/IPv4-literal hardening (P1-06 comment) never fires because no literal IP is present. Fix requires resolving the host and re-checking every resolved address (or pinning the connection) rather than parsing the host string as an IP.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:352-357 — processQueue() permanently DROPS a terminally-failed offline mutation from the sync queue with only a `console.error('Action failed after max retries:', action)`. An action is terminal when it is `permanent` (a 4xx, reasonable to drop) OR `action.retries >= 3` (transient 5xx/network — NOT safe to drop). At line ~400 the queue is rebuilt keeping only `!succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)`, so the failed action's PAYLOAD (e.g. an offline-created fault report from screens/faults/ReportFaultScreen.tsx, or a document action) is discarded with no dead-letter store and no per-item retry affordance.

Surfacing is aggregate-only: App.tsx:82 fires processQueue() fire-and-forget on reconnect; syncProgress.failed (App.tsx:334) feeds PendingSyncIndicator.tsx which renders a t('sync.failed') count. The user sees 'N failed' but cannot see WHICH items failed nor recover/re-submit them — after 3 transient-failure sync cycles genuine user work is silently lost even though the server may have only been temporarily unavailable.

Reachability traced: App.tsx onReconnect useEffect -> processQueue -> per-action executeQueuedAction catch -> retries++ -> retries>=3 terminal drop. Confidence medium (static; the 4xx branch is intentional and correct, the transient-exhaustion branch is the data-loss concern). Suggested fix: move retry-exhausted (non-permanent) actions to a persisted dead-letter list with an explicit user-visible 'retry / discard' surface rather than dropping them, and/or exempt idempotent CREATEs from the 3-cycle cap.
